source_text: ἀνὴρ δίκαιος καὶ φοβούμενος τὸν θεόν, μαρ τυρούμενός τε ὑπὸ παντὸς ἔθνους τῶν Ἰουδαίων, ἐχρηματίσθη ὑπὸ ἀγ γέλου ἁγίου, μεταμέμψασθαί σε εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀκοῦσαι ῥή ματα παρὰ σοῦ.» ὑμεῖς μὲν οὖν, εἰ ἐσιωπήσατε καὶ ἀπερράψατε συκοφαντίας τὰ στόματα, ἐπράττετε ἂν πολλῷ λυσιτελέστερον. ἡμεῖς δὲ ἐπὶ τὸν τελειότερον σκοπὸν ἀναπέμποντες καὶ τὸ κεφάλαιον τοῦτο καὶ εὐθυμίαν τοῖς ἐντευξομένοις παρέχοντες καὶ πλείονα τὸν ὀρθόδοξον ζῆλον ἐμβάλλοντες φαμέν, ὅτι ὡς οὐδεμία κοινωνία φύσεως κτίσματι πρὸς τὴν ἄκτιστον φύσιν ἐστίν, οὕτως οὐδὲ χρηματισμοῦ. ὁ μὲν γὰρ ἀγγέλλει, ὁ δ' ἂν οὐκ εἰδὼς ὑπὸ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος εἰπεῖν ἐνεργηθείη, καὶ ἐντεῦθεν αὐτῷ ἄγγελος τοὔνομα· τὸ δὲ ἅγιον πνεῦμα ἅτε πάντα εἰδὸς τὰ τοῦ θεοῦ, ὡς διαβεβαιοῦται ὁ Παῦλος, χρηματίζει θεϊκῶς, ὡς ὁ πατήρ, ἅπερ ἂν τοῖς τῆς θεότητος ἀκοιμήτοις ὄμμασιν ὁρᾷ βουλόμενον καὶ τὸν πατέρα καὶ τὸν υἱὸν καὶ οὐ διακονικῶς, καθάπερ ὁ δορυφόρος ἄγγελος. «ὁ γὰρ δοῦλος οὐκ οἶδεν, τί ποιεῖ ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ», οὐδέ γε ὁ ἑτεροούσιος τὴν αὐτὴν τῷ ἑτέρας ὄντι οὐσίας κεκτῆσθαι δύναται γνῶσιν· φύσει γὰρ ἑκάστῃ ἡ ἀνήκουσα γνῶσις καὶ μνήμη συμπαρομαρτεῖ· ἀλλὰ καὶ τὸ γνωσθὲν τῇ γενητῇ φύσει ἔσθ' ὅτε τῷ χρόνῳ ἀφίπταται. ὅθεν κἀνταῦθα τὴν ἀρχὴν τοῦ χωρίου ἑκόντες ἐν τῇ διαμάχῃ τοῦ λόγου παραλελοίπασιν οἱ ἀγνώμονες. ἔχει γάρ· «τοῦ δὲ Πέτρου διενθυμουμένου περὶ τοῦ ῥήματος εἶπεν αὐτῷ τὲ ἅγιον πνεῦμα· ἰδοὺ ἄνδρες τρεῖς ζητοῦσίν σε. ἀλλὰ ἀναστὰς πορεύθητι σὺν αὐτοῖς, μηδὲν διακρινόμενος· διότι ἐγὼ ἀπέσταλκα αὐτούς. καταβὰς δὲ Πέτρος πρὸς τοὺς ἄνδρας εἶπεν· ἰδοὺ ἐγώ, ὃν ζητεῖτε· τίς ἡ αἰτία δι' ἣν πάρεστε; οἱ δὲ εἶπαν· Κορνήλιος ἑκατοντάρχης, ἀνὴρ δίκαιος», καὶ τὰ ἑξῆς, ὡς πρόκειται. ὥστε παρὰ κριταῖς ἀγαθοῖς κἀνταῦθα παρὰ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος φαίνεται τὸν χρησμὸν ὁ ἄγγελος μαθών. θεότητος γὰρ ἔκκριτον γνώρισμα τὸ προλέγειν ἀσφάλτως· καὶ τοῦτο ἐπ' ἀγαθῷ τῶν ἀκουόντων, ἵν' ἀσφαλισάμενοι σωθῶσιν. εἶτα οὐ νομίζετε τοιαῦτα εἰσηγούμενοι βασκαίνειν μέν πως τῇ κτίσει, μέμφεσθαι δὲ οἷον τῷ δι' ἀφθονίαν ταῖς περὶ αὐτοῦ εἰρημέναις λέξεσιν κοσμήσαντι τὰ ἑαυτοῦ ποιήματα; ὡς ἑπομένης πάντως τῷ τοιούτῳ πράγματι καὶ τῆς αὐτοῦ χάριτος. ἐκ γὰρ καὶ τούτου ὕβρισεν μὲν ἑαυτὸν οὐδαμῶς, μᾶλλον δὲ καὶ ἐπαινετὸν ἔδειξεν, τὰ δὲ ἔργα αὐτοῦ συνήθως ἐφαίδρυνεν. ἡμεῖς δέ, εἰ καὶ σεμνότητά τινα θείαν τῇ πάσῃ ὑποθέσει φέρει τὸ χρηματίζειν τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα, καὶ ἀρκεῖ καθ' ἑαυτὸ παραλαμβανόμενον εἰς μαρτυρίαν, ὅμως οὐ μόνον αὐτό, ἀλλὰ γὰρ καὶ πλῆθος ἄλλο ὑψηλῶν καὶ ἀναμφισβητήτων ἀποδείξεων παρηγάγομεν· οἷς εἰ προσέχετε ἀντιπαθείας ἄνευ, ἀφωνότεροι πάντως ἔσεσθε τῶν ἰχθύων. διελέγχει τοίνυν τὴν πιθανουργίαν ὑμῶν σαφέστατα καὶ ὁ Παῦλος, Ἐφεσίοις γράψας· «ἐμοὶ τῷ ἐλαχιστοτέρῳ πάντων ἁγίων ἐδόθη ἡ χάρις αὕτη ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν εὐαγγελίσασθαι τὸν ἀνεξιχνίαστον πλοῦτον τοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ φωτίσαι πάντας, τίς ἡ οἰκονομία τοῦ μυστηρίου τοῦ ἀποκεκρυμμένου ἀπὸ τῶν αἰώνων ἐν τῷ θεῷ τῷ τὰ πάντα κτίσαντι· ἵνα γνωρισθῇ νῦν ταῖς ἀρχαῖς καὶ ταῖς ἐξουσίαις ἐν τοῖς ἐπουρανίοις διὰ τῆς ἐκ κλησίας ἡ πολυποίκιλος σοφία τοῦ θεοῦ.» κατανοεῖτε οὖν, πόσον ἐξῄρηται ἡ ἀγγέλων φύσις τοῦ ἀφ' ἑαυτῆς εἰδέναι τι τῶν ἐσομένων καὶ τοῦ χρηματίζειν· ὅτι καὶ διὰ τῆς ἐν τῷδε τῷ κόσμῳ ἐκκλησίας τοῦ 75 θεοῦ, ἥτις ἐσμὲν ἡμεῖς, τὰ μεγαλεῖα μανθάνει. πρὸς πειθὼ δὲ τὴν περὶ τοῦτο δύναταί τι συλλαμβάνειν καὶ ἅπερ Κολοσσαεῦσιν ἔγραψεν τοιῶσδε· «τὸ μυστήριον τοῦτο τὸ ἀποκεκρυμμένον πρὸ τῶν αἰώνων καὶ ἀπὸ τῶν γενεῶν, ὃ νῦν ἐφανερώθη τοῖς ἁγίοις αὐτοῦ.» πρὸ τούτου γάρ, φησίν, τῷ θεῷ ἔγνωστο μόνῳ. πρὸς τούτοις καὶ ἅπερ περὶ τῶν ἐνεγκόντων πᾶσιν ἀνθρώποις ὄφελος, τῶν περὶ τὴν ἄλεκτον οἰκονομίαν φημί, τοῖσδε παρὰ Πέτρου ἀνείρηται τοῖς ῥητοῖς, ὡς προελέχθη· «εἰς ἅ», φησίν, «ἐπιθυμοῦσιν ἄγγελοι παρακύψαι.» εἰ δέ τινα ἔμφυτον γνῶσιν εἶχον, οὐκ ἂν ἱμείροντο τοῦ κἂν διακύψαι εἰς αὐτό, ἀλλ' ἐπειδὴ μὴ ἔχουσιν, εἰς ὑπερβάλλοντα, ὡς οἱ ἄνθρωποι, τρόπον τινὰ ἐκπίπτουσιν ἔρωτα ἐκείνων, ὧν τῆς γνώσεως τυχεῖν αὐτοῖς μὴ ὕπεστιν. πέφυκεν γὰρ καὶ τὴν ἄλλως ὑπερορᾶσθαι μὲν τὰ εὑρεθῆναι ῥᾴδια, ποιεῖσθαι δὲ τὰ σπανιώτερα. καὶ μέντοι καὶ τοῦτο οὐ κατὰ γνώμην οἰκείαν, τῷ κοινῷ δὲ τῆς φύσεως αὐτῶν λόγῳ οὐ πάντας φημί ὑπόχρεοι ὄντες τινές. «εἰ γάρ», φησίν, «ἀγγέλων ἁμαρτησάντων ὁ θεὸς οὐκ ἐφείσατο», ποίαν ἔμφυτον γνῶσιν τῶν
pass_a_gloss: [Continuing the quotation of Acts 10:22 from the previous section: 'Cornelius, a centurion,] a man righteous and fearing God, and being testified to by all the nation of the Jews, was divinely instructed by a holy angel to summon you to his house and to hear words from you.' You, then, if you had kept silent and sewn up the mouths of slander, would have fared much more profitably. But we, referring this chapter too to the more perfect aim, and providing good cheer to those who will read [it], and putting in more orthodox zeal, say that, as there is no communion of nature for a creature with the uncreated nature, so neither of giving revelation. For the one [the angel] announces whatever, not knowing [it], he may be moved by the Holy Spirit to say, and hence his name is angel; but the Holy Spirit, inasmuch as knowing all the things of God, as Paul affirms, gives revelation in a godly way, as the Father, whatever he sees with the sleepless eyes of the Godhead [that he is] willing, and [that] both the Father and the Son [will], and not in a serving way, as the bodyguard angel. 'For the slave does not know what his lord does'; nor indeed can the one of another essence have acquired the same knowledge as the one being of a different essence; for to each nature the knowledge and memory belonging to it accompanies [it]; but even what has been known by the created nature sometimes flies off with time. Hence here too the unfair ones have willingly left out the beginning of the passage in the fight of the argument. For it has: 'And while Peter was pondering about the word, the Holy Spirit said to him [the print has τὲ, read τὸ]: behold, three men seek you. But rising, go with them, doubting nothing; because I have sent them. And Peter, having gone down to the men, said: behold, I am the one whom you seek; what is the cause for which you are present? And they said: Cornelius, a centurion, a righteous man,' and the things in order, as is set out above. So that before good judges here too the angel appears to have learned the oracle from the Holy Spirit. For an exceptional mark of Godhead [is] foretelling unerringly; and this for the good of those who hear, that having been made secure they may be saved. Then do you not think, introducing such things, that you somehow begrudge the creation, and, as it were, blame the one who through generosity adorned his own works with the words spoken about himself? As his grace too surely following such a thing. For from this too he in no way insulted himself, but rather showed [himself] praiseworthy too, and brightened his works as is his custom. But we, even if the Holy Spirit's giving revelation brings some divine majesty to the whole subject, and suffices taken by itself for testimony, nevertheless have brought forward not it alone, but indeed also another multitude of lofty and indisputable proofs; to which if you attend without hostility, you will surely be more voiceless than the fish. Paul too, then, most clearly refutes your plausible-dealing, having written to Ephesians: 'To me, the less than least of all saints, this grace was given, among the gentiles to preach the untraceable wealth of Christ and to enlighten all what is the economy of the mystery that had been hidden from the ages in God who created all things; that now may be made known to the principalities and to the authorities in the heavenly [places] through the church the much-varied wisdom of God.' Consider then how much the nature of angels is removed from knowing of itself anything of the things to come and from giving revelation; since even through the church of God in this world, which we are, [page number 75, debris] it learns the great things. And toward persuasion about this, those things too which he wrote to Colossians thus can contribute something: 'this mystery that had been hidden before the ages and from the generations, which now was made manifest to his saints.' For before this, he says, it had been known to God alone. Besides these also the things which, about the things that brought benefit to all men, I mean those about the unspeakable economy, have been declared by Peter in these words, as was said before: 'into which,' he says, 'angels desire to stoop and look.' But if they had some innate knowledge, they would not long even to peer into it; but since they do not have [it], they fall in a certain way, as men [do], into an excessive desire of those things whose knowledge it is not within them to obtain. For it is natural also otherwise that things easy to be found are overlooked, but the rarer are made much of. And yet this too [is] not according to their own judgment, but some, I do not say all, being liable to the common principle of their nature. 'For if,' he says, 'God did not spare angels who sinned,' what innate knowledge of the [continues in the next section] ...
pass_b_english: …a righteous man who fears God, well spoken of by the whole nation of the Jews, received a revelation from a holy angel to send for you to come to his house and to hear words from you’” (Acts 10:22). As for you, if you had kept silent and stitched shut your slandering mouths, you would have done yourselves far more good.

But we refer this chapter too to the more perfect aim; we give good cheer to those who will read it, and we instil a greater zeal for the orthodox faith. So we say that, just as a creature has no communion of nature with the uncreated nature, so neither has it communion in giving revelation. For the angel announces whatever he is moved by the Holy Spirit to say without knowing it himself, and that is why his name is “angel,” that is, messenger. But the Holy Spirit, since he knows all the things of God, as Paul affirms (1 Corinthians 2:10–11), gives revelation in the manner of God, as the Father does: whatever he sees with the sleepless eyes of the Godhead that he wills, and that the Father and the Son will. He does not do it as a servant, as the angel of the guard does. “For the servant does not know what his master is doing” (John 15:15); nor indeed can one of another essence possess the same knowledge as one who is of a different essence. For to each nature belong the knowledge and the memory proper to it; and even what a created nature has come to know sometimes flies away with time.

That is why here too these unfair men have deliberately left out the beginning of the passage in the heat of their argument. For it runs: “While Peter was pondering the matter, the Holy Spirit said to him: ‘Behold, three men are looking for you. Rise, then, and go with them without any doubting, for I have sent them.’ And Peter went down to the men and said: ‘Behold, I am the one you are looking for. What is the reason you have come?’ And they said: ‘Cornelius, a centurion, a righteous man’” (Acts 10:19–22), and the rest, as set out above. So, before fair judges, here too the angel is plainly seen to have learned the oracle from the Holy Spirit. For to foretell without error is the distinctive mark of the Godhead; and this is for the good of those who hear, so that, being made secure, they may be saved.

Then do you not see that by bringing in such ideas you somehow begrudge the creation, and find fault, as it were, with him who out of his generosity adorned his own works with the words spoken of himself? For his grace surely goes with such a gift. And by this he in no way dishonoured himself; rather he showed himself worthy of praise, and, as is his custom, made his works shine.

As for us: even though the Holy Spirit’s giving of revelation lends a certain divine majesty to the whole subject, and is enough as testimony when taken by itself, we have still brought forward not that alone, but a whole host of other lofty and indisputable proofs. If you attend to them without hostility, you will surely be more speechless than the fish.

Paul too, then, refutes your plausible trickery most clearly, writing to the Ephesians: “To me, who am less than the least of all the saints, this grace was given: to preach among the Gentiles the unsearchable riches of Christ, and to bring to light for all what is the plan of the mystery hidden from the ages in God, who created all things, so that the manifold wisdom of God might now be made known through the church to the principalities and the powers in the heavenly places” (Ephesians 3:8–10). Consider, then, how far the nature of the angels is removed from knowing anything of the future by itself, and from giving revelation: it learns the great things even through the church of God in this world, which is ourselves. And what he wrote to the Colossians can also help somewhat to persuade on this point. He writes: “This mystery, which was hidden before the ages and from the generations, but has now been revealed to his saints” (Colossians 1:26). For before this, he means, it was known to God alone.

Besides these, there is what Peter declared, as was said before, about the things that brought benefit to all men (I mean the things of the unspeakable plan of salvation), in these words: “Into which,” he says, “angels long to look” (1 Peter 1:12). But if they had some innate knowledge, they would not long even to peer into it. Since they do not have it, they fall, in a way, as men do, into an overwhelming desire for things whose knowledge is not within their reach. For it is natural in other matters too that what is easy to find is overlooked, while what is rarer is prized. And yet this too is not by any choice of their own; rather, by the common law of their nature some of them, though I do not say all, are subject to it. “For if,” he says, “God did not spare angels when they sinned” (2 Peter 2:4), what innate knowledge of the …

(passive) be moved, be set to work

choices.issue: Garbled machine draft, one sentence split, Ephesians cited at the wrong verse
choices.choice: 2026-11-11 (claude-sumfix2-e-u18): retranslated. The old English had Cornelius 'brought into his house', read ὃ δ' ἂν ('whatever') as 'the other', had the Spirit '[inform] the Father and the Son', wrote 'the knowledge not belonging to it and memory are co-participating in error', 'rushing into the field of the battle of the Word, have gone astray', 'less speechless than the fish', 'the unchosen economy' and 'this is raised by Peter to the rhetoricians', and split 'since his grace surely goes with such a gift' off as the orphan 'And of his grace.' References: (Eph 3:8) -> Ephesians 3:8-10, since the quotation runs through 3:10; (Col 1:26), (1 Pet 1:12), (2 Pet 2:4) written in full; the three Acts 10 references merged into Acts 10:19-22; Acts 10:22 (opening words) and 1 Corinthians 2:10-11 added. Brackets [us], [communion], [mere], [informs], [possess] removed.

choices.why: The quotation opened at the end of the previous section ('Cornelius, a centurion, …'); this section holds its close, so it opens with '…' and is cited here.
Literally 'sewn up the mouths of slander'; the mouths are the opponents' own.

choices.term: ὁ μὲν γὰρ ἀγγέλλει, ὃ δ' ἂν οὐκ εἰδὼς ... εἰπεῖν ἐνεργηθείη
choices.english: the angel announces whatever he is moved by the Holy Spirit to say without knowing it himself
choices.why: Read as ὃ δ' ἄν, 'whatever'; Didymus' point is that the messenger passes on what he does not know of himself. The pun on ἀγγέλλει / ἄγγελος is kept with 'angel, that is, messenger'.

choices.term: ἅπερ ἂν ... ὁρᾷ βουλόμενον καὶ τὸν πατέρα καὶ τὸν υἱὸν
choices.english: whatever he sees with the sleepless eyes of the Godhead that he wills, and that the Father and the Son will
choices.why: Loose syntax: βουλόμενον agrees with the Spirit, and the accusatives 'the Father and the Son' are read as sharing the same will. The Spirit speaks what the Trinity wills, not as a messenger.
δορυφόρος is a bodyguard who attends a king; the angel serves, the Spirit does not.
Clear allusion to 'the Spirit searches all things' and 'no one knows the things of God except the Spirit of God'.

choices.term: ὁ γὰρ δοῦλος οὐκ οἶδεν, τί ποιεῖ ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ
choices.english: “For the servant does not know what his master is doing” (John 15:15)
choices.why: Quotation of John 15:15; 'servant' and 'master' fit Didymus' contrast with the serving angel.
ἀνήκουσα means belonging, fitting; the old 'not belonging to it' reversed it.
Didymus' text reads ῥήματος where Acts 10:19 has ὁράματος (vision); the English follows his word.
τὲ is a misprint for τό in the copy-text.

choices.term: μέμφεσθαι ... τῷ δι' ἀφθονίαν ταῖς περὶ αὐτοῦ εἰρημέναις λέξεσιν κοσμήσαντι τὰ ἑαυτοῦ ποιήματα
choices.english: find fault with him who out of his generosity adorned his own works with the words spoken of himself
choices.why: God freely lends words used of himself (here 'give revelation') to his creatures; denying the Spirit's deity because an angel shares the word blames the giver.

choices.english: For his grace surely goes with such a gift.
choices.why: A genitive absolute ending the sentence; the old English printed it as the fragment 'And of his grace.'
Comparative; the old 'less speechless' reversed it.
In Ephesians 3:9 the plan of the mystery; in the Peter sentence 'the unspeakable economy' is the plan of salvation in Christ, so 'plan of salvation' is used there.

choices.term: ἵνα γνωρισθῇ νῦν ταῖς ἀρχαῖς ... διὰ τῆς ἐκκλησίας
choices.english: so that the manifold wisdom of God might now be made known through the church to the principalities and the powers
choices.why: This is Ephesians 3:10, so the reference covers 3:8-10, not 3:8 alone (reader report).

choices.english: “Into which,” he says, “angels long to look” (1 Peter 1:12)
choices.why: παρακύπτω is to stoop and peer in; Didymus plays on it with διακύψαι, 'peer into it'.

choices.term: τὴν ἄλλως ... ποιεῖσθαι δὲ τὰ σπανιώτερα
choices.english: in other matters too ... what is rarer is prized
choices.why: ποιεῖσθαι is short for 'make much of'; 'prized' gives the contrast with 'overlooked'.

choices.term: οὐ κατὰ γνώμην οἰκείαν, τῷ κοινῷ δὲ τῆς φύσεως αὐτῶν λόγῳ οὐ πάντας φημί ὑπόχρεοι ὄντες τινές
choices.english: this too is not by any choice of their own; rather, by the common law of their nature some of them, though I do not say all, are subject to it
choices.why: Compressed syntax; read as: the angels' ignorance and longing come from their created nature, to which some (the fallen, as 2 Peter 2:4 shows next) are liable. Flagged in problems.
75 is a printed page number in the copy-text, skipped.
The sentence runs into the next section (μελλόντων, 'things to come'); only the words this section holds are translated, ending with '…'.

choices.english: who am less than the least
choices.why: A comparative built on a superlative; English keeps Paul's double form.
